title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the unpublished continuation (pp. 650bis–787) of La Longue Marche. It sits between p. 717 and p. 718, so it is presumably 717'. On p. 717 Grothendieck says that his 'preceding theorems' clarify, in terms of the Fermat tower, the arithmetic-geometric meaning of a homomorphism M = N_{1,1}^{ét} → G_{ρ,σ} ≃ Ẑ^*·𝔖^{+∧}. That homomorphism had been obtained 'by purely algebraic means' in section 11. He also considers the weaker map M̃ = M/μ_M → G̃_{ρ,σ} = G_{ρ,σ}/μ. Here G̃_{ρ,σ} is an extension of F̃ = Ẑ^* × 𝔖_3 by an abelian profinite module M̂.

Step 1 (this page). Combine this with the vanishing H^0(Ẑ^*×𝔖_3, M̂) = H^1(Ẑ^*×𝔖_3, M̂) = 0.
- H^1 = 0 makes the extension G̃ split, with all splittings conjugate.
- H^0 = 0 makes the conjugating element unique.
- So G̃ ≅ M̂ ⋊ (Ẑ^*×𝔖_3) canonically. It can be read as a group of (affine) transformations of a profinite set or space E (the reading of what E is, 'l'un E de ses ...', is uncertain).

Step 2. A continuous homomorphism from M̃ to the transformation group of E is the same thing as an action of M̃ on E. Grothendieck identifies M̃ = π_1(U_{0,3,ℚ}, 𝔖_3) = π_1(M'_{1,1,ℚ}). This is the arithmetic fundamental group of the orbifold (P^1−{0,1,∞})/𝔖_3, i.e. the λ-line modulo 𝔖_3 = SL_2(𝔽_2). That quotient is the j-line with the generic ±1 removed (rigidified M_{1,1}), whose geometric π_1 is PSL_2(ℤ)^∧ ⊃ F̂_2 with quotient 𝔖_3. So the action corresponds to a profinite (pro-)covering of (U_{0,3,ℚ}, 𝔖_3) ≃ M'_{1,1,ℚ}. He states that this pro-covering is exactly the Fermat pro-covering, i.e. the tower of Fermat curves x^n + y^n = 1 over P^1−{0,1,∞}:
- its geometric Galois group is Ẑ^2 = π_{0,3}^{ab};
- the 𝔖_3 symmetry permutes the three punctures;
- Galois acts through the cyclotomic character Ẑ^*.
On this reading M̂ is presumably the 'Tate module of the Fermat tower', i.e. a metabelian piece π'/π'' of π_{0,3}.

Step 3. What remains is to interpret the full map M = N_{1,1} → G_{ρ,σ} in the same way. It sits in the morphism of exact sequences (298):
- top row: 1 → μ_M = {1,ω} → M (N''_{1,1}) → M̃ (N'_{1,1} = M_{0,3}) → 1;
- bottom row: 1 → μ_G = {1,ω} → G_{ρ,σ} → G̃_{ρ,σ} → 1;
- the left vertical map is an isomorphism.
Here ω is presumably the central involution (−1). So M is the pullback of the central extension G_{ρ,σ} along M̃ → G̃_{ρ,σ}.

Step 4 (next page). This is explicitly compared with an earlier construction (§48). There, M = N_{1,1}, essentially SL_2-type, was reconstructed as the pullback of GL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1} along M_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}. That map came from the 'Lie-type' quotient SL(2,Ẑ)' of π_{0,3}^{+∧}. So both the 'Lie/elliptic' (GL_2) quotient and the 'Fermat/metabelian' quotient recover the central ±1 extension by pullback. Grothendieck frames all this as making anabelian-geometric aspects explicit through automorphisms of profinite structures based on π_{0,3}^∧.

What the page serves. It tries to give a geometric meaning (a specific tower of covers of the modular orbifold) to a homomorphism found algebraically. That is, it identifies the Fermat tower as the covering classified by M̃ → G̃_{ρ,σ}.
errors: The claimed vanishing H^0 = H^1 = 0 for Ẑ^*×𝔖_3 acting on M̂ needs care at the prime 2. The usual 'central-element trick' (−1 ∈ Ẑ^* acting by −1, or a scalar λ with λ−1 invertible) only kills cohomology away from 2. At 2 no λ ∈ ℤ_2^* has λ−1 a unit, so H^1 could have 2-torsion unless the 𝔖_3 action or the precise module structure is used. The page gives no argument, so this is an unverified assertion.
The word 'permettrait' (conditional) signals a heuristic. The identification of the covering with the Fermat pro-covering is asserted, not proved, on this page.
Notation drifts between pages: G_{ρ,σ} vs G_{φ,σ}, and M vs M̃ (p. 717 notes that M̃ was written M on earlier pages). The meaning of E is not determinable from the image.

ideas.what: Using H^0 = H^1 = 0 to rigidify an extension of Ẑ^*×𝔖_3 by M̂ into a canonical semidirect product, i.e. a transformation group, so that a homomorphism into it becomes a profinite covering.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomological rigidity of split extensions; classification of étale (pro-)coverings by continuous π_1-sets
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (Galois theory of π_1); the cohomological rigidity itself is standard

ideas.what: Identifying (P^1−{0,1,∞})/𝔖_3 with the rigidified modular orbifold M'_{1,1}, with π_1 = PSL_2-type extension of 𝔖_3 by F̂_2, and arithmetic π_1 over ℚ.
ideas.modern_name: λ-line as level-2 modular curve; M_{1,1} = [M_{0,4}/𝔖_3] up to ±1 gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre/Klein); in anabelian form Grothendieck, Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), the Teichmüller tower M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}

ideas.what: Interpreting an algebraically obtained homomorphism from the arithmetic modular group into Ẑ^*·(metabelian completion of 𝔖-extension) as the Galois/monodromy action on the Fermat tower over P^1−{0,1,∞}.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the Fermat tower / metabelian quotient π'/π'' of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}); Ihara's universal power series for Jacobi sums
ideas.usually_credited_to: Y. Ihara (Annals 1986, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'); G. Anderson (hyperadelic gamma function, 1989); Coleman
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) discusses the Fermat tower; the specific link to G_{ρ,σ} seems to be only in these unpublished continuation pages

ideas.what: Recovering the central ±1 extension M = N_{1,1} (SL_2-type) of M_{0,3}-type group as a pullback of a central extension of the target. This is done in parallel for a 'Lie-type' quotient (GL_2(Ẑ)) and for the Fermat/metabelian quotient.
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of central extensions; SL_2(ℤ)^∧ → PSL_2(ℤ)^∧ via the elliptic Tate-module representation
ideas.where_published: Possibly earlier unpublished parts of the Longue Marche sequel (§48)

missed.claim: Around 1981 Grothendieck appears to identify a homomorphism from the arithmetic modular group π_1(M'_{1,1,ℚ}) into an explicit group Ẑ^*·(metabelian 𝔖_3-structure) as the monodromy/Galois action on the Fermat pro-covering. He sets it in parallel with the GL_2(Ẑ) (elliptic Tate module) representation, both recovering the central ±1 extension by pullback. This anticipates the Ihara–Anderson–Coleman study of Galois action on the Fermat tower (metabelian quotient of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞})) and treats it uniformly with the elliptic GL_2 picture over the modular orbifold. The literature usually credits that study to Ihara (1985–86) and does not present it in this M_{1,1}/𝔖_3-equivariant, 'two quotients of π_{0,3}' form.
missed.quote: correspondant donc à un revêtement profini de (U_{0,3 Q}, S_3) ≃ M_{1,1}'_Q - et ce revêtement n'est autre que le prorevêtement de Fermat.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical priority point. It also suggests viewing the Fermat/Jacobi-sum (metabelian) Galois representation and the elliptic GL_2 representation as two parallel 'linearizations' of π_1(M_{1,1}). This framing is relevant to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller / elliptic GT and metabelian GT literature.

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open a geometric interpretation of the full map N_{1,1} → G_{ρ,σ}, as opposed to its quotient modulo μ. He proposes reading it via a pullback of the central extension, but this is not carried out here.
missed.quote: Il resterait à interpréter de façon analogue l'homom. M=N_{1,1} → G_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This amounts to describing the ±1 gerbe over the Fermat tower's monodromy group (a metaplectic-type lift). It is a modest open thread that is probably easy for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck interest in the Fermat tower is known from La Longue Marche. The detail that is notable but unpublished is the explicit identification of an algebraically constructed map from π_1(M'_{1,1,ℚ}) with the Fermat pro-covering, combined with the parallel to the GL_2(Ẑ) pullback construction. This prefigures Ihara's work, but the page is heuristic and the core facts are now standard.
transcription_corrections: 'n'est autre que la prorevêtement' should read 'n'est autre que le prorevêtement de Fermat'.
This page is probably numbered 717' or 717bis; the archive number 139 is the scan index.
In (298) the right-hand top entry is labelled '(N'_{1,1} = M_{0,3})' with an arrow down to G̃_{ρ,σ}; the left vertical arrow carries ≀ (isomorphism) between μ_M = {1,ω} and μ_G = {1,ω}.
The phrase rendered 'sur l'une E de ses pro-groupes [?] ...' is very uncertain in the image; it is possibly 'sur l'un E de ses ... [torseurs/points]'. E is some profinite space on which G̃ acts.
In the inserted line, 'comme une [-hom-] quotient de M' is likely 'comme une {+quotient+}' (struck 'hom'); the following line reads 'de M̃ = π_1(U_{0,3 Q}, 𝔖_3) = π_1(M'_{1,1 Q}) sur E'.
